about.title: Eureka Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product doesn't announce itself before it fails — a ladder that snaps, a space heater that sparks a fire, a car part that gives out on Broadway Street or Rt 101. Humboldt County residents rely on everyday goods from tools to appliances to vehicle components, and when one of those items is poorly designed, badly manufactured, or missing a proper warning, the people who get hurt shouldn't have to prove the company was careless. California's strict liability rules generally focus on whether the product itself was defective and whether that defect caused harm. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects injured Eureka residents with an independent personal injury attorney familiar with these claims. If a product hurt you or someone in your household, the item itself, packaging, and any receipts matter, and an attorney can help you understand what to do next at no upfront cost.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, which generally focuses on whether the product had a defect and whether that defect caused the injury, rather than requiring proof of carelessness. An independent attorney can review your situation and explain how this might apply to your case.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to preserve the item exactly as it was when the injury happened, along with any packaging, manuals, or receipts. This evidence can matter a great deal later, and an attorney can advise on safe storage and documentation.

If a faulty product contributed to an injury in one of these situations, it's worth having it evaluated.
